coverage_gaps: Only PubMed is available, so trial registries, preprint servers, regulator databases, patent sources and independent citation graphs cannot be searched directly.
PubMed-only expansion may miss forward citations, non-indexed conference material, very recent preprints and records with sparse title or abstract terminology.
Full-text availability and non-English screening capacity are unspecified, which may limit verification of methods, negative results and exact variant or substrate context.
Publication-date ambiguity for online-first articles and corrections may remain when PubMed metadata does not expose all relevant dates.
The fixed 12-query budget limits iterative alias repair and a second independent expansion route if sentinel recovery or challenge screening reveals an unexpected terminology gap.
exclusion_criteria: Records first published after 2024-12-31 are excluded from the evidence set and logged as post-cutoff.
Records that only mention LRRK2 or Parkinson disease without direct genetic, enzymatic, substrate or physiological evidence are excluded.
Editorials, narrative reviews and unsourced opinions are excluded as final claim-supporting evidence.
Purely computational substrate or variant predictions lacking experimental or human genetic validation are excluded from mechanistic support.
Studies of LRRK2 outside Parkinson disease are excluded when they provide no transferable evidence about enzyme function, substrate biology or disease-relevant physiology.
Experiments using only overexpression or nonselective pharmacology are excluded from strong physiological-substrate support unless accompanied by orthogonal endogenous or genetic controls.
Records with unresolved identity, irreconcilable metadata or inaccessible evidence needed to verify the reported mechanism are excluded from synthesis and retained in the screening ledger.
Duplicate presentations of the same canonical record are merged without deleting their query, wave or provenance links.
inclusion_criteria: Publication date is on or before 2024-12-31 after reconciling electronic, issue and correction dates in PubMed metadata.
Primary human genetic studies directly addressing LRRK2 linkage, segregation, pathogenicity, association, penetrance, ancestry or phenotype are eligible.

Biochemical, structural, cellular or animal studies are eligible when they directly manipulate or measure LRRK2 catalytic state, a proposed substrate or a mechanistically linked physiological outcome.
Substrate claims require traceable evidence for direct phosphorylation or dependence on LRRK2 activity; endogenous, genetic-loss, knock-in, patient-derived or human-tissue evidence receives priority.
Null, negative, conflicting, replication, correction and retraction records relevant to a high-impact claim are retained and labeled.
All organisms and languages are eligible when the record has sufficient PubMed metadata for screening; organism and model are carried into evidence grading.
Reviews and perspectives are eligible for terminology and citation mining, while final mechanistic claims must trace to primary records.
Records are deduplicated by PMID and DOI while every query-to-record occurrence and retrieval wave is preserved.

queries.purpose: Recover landmark human genetic-discovery records and the landmark phosphoproteomic Rab-substrate record, validating PARK8, dardarin, LRRK2 and Rab terminology before broad retrieval.
queries.query: ((((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR dardarin[Title/Abstract]) AND Parkinson*[Title/Abstract] AND ((Zimprich[Author] AND 2004[Date - Publication]) OR (Paisan-Ruiz[Author] AND 2004[Date - Publication]))) OR (LRRK2[Title/Abstract] AND Rab[Title/Abstract] AND Steger[Author] AND 2016[Date - Publication])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication]))

queries.purpose: Refresh all decision-critical branches through the delivery cutoff and capture recent online-first genetic, structural, substrate and human-validation studies.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR "leucine-rich repeat kinase 2"[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Parkinson Disease"[Mesh] OR Parkinson*[Title/Abstract]) AND (variant*[Title/Abstract] OR penetrance[Title/Abstract] OR kinase[Title/Abstract] OR GTPase[Title/Abstract] OR substrate*[Title/Abstract] OR Rab[Title/Abstract] OR phosphoproteom*[Title/Abstract] OR lysosom*[Title/Abstract] OR mechanism*[Title/Abstract])) AND ("2022/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: In Parkinson disease, how did human genetics identify LRRK2, which pathogenic or risk variants are supported across populations, how do kinase and ROC-COR GTPase functions connect variants to altered activity, which endogenous physiological substrates and pathways are supported, and what negative, variant-specific, model-dependent, tissue-dependent or population-dependent evidence limits a unified mechanism? Scope is PubMed-indexed literature from database inception through 2024-12-31, prioritizing human genetics, patient-derived material and human tissue, while admitting biochemical, structural, cellular and animal studies needed for causal mechanism. All languages are eligible; peer-reviewed primary studies support claims, while reviews support terminology and citation expansion. Outcomes include variant causality, risk, penetrance, catalytic effects, endogenous substrate phosphorylation, downstream physiology and evidence generalizability.
stop_rules: Execute no more than the 12 specified PubMed query events and record each exact query, execution timestamp, result count, requested cutoff and available provider-version information.
Do not stop broad retrieval until the 2004 genetic-discovery anchors and the 2016 Rab-substrate anchor are recovered or a failed anchor check and attempted alias correction are documented.
Complete sentinel, discovery, confirmation, expansion, challenge and update waves before synthesis unless the query-event cap is exhausted.

Require direct primary evidence for genetic discovery, variant interpretation, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrates and at least one limitation to each high-impact claim family before declaring coverage sufficient.
Stop adaptive expansion when two consecutive screened expansion batches add no new decision-relevant variant, mechanism, substrate or limiting evidence.
Apply the publication cutoff after retrieval when PubMed indexing or online-first dates are ambiguous, and exclude any unresolved post-cutoff record from claim support.
At the 12-event cap, stop retrieval, preserve unresolved branches in coverage_gaps and avoid replacing missing evidence with inference.
Stop screening when remaining unscreened records cannot change the direction, confidence or stated generality of any planned claim, with that judgment documented by branch.
